findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employees not using a barriers to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was corrected. Endure that the appropriate procedures for handwashing are followed always to avoid recontaminating your hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.comment: The soda nozzles were observed with an accumulation of soil. PIC was made aware. PIC removed the soda nozzles and began cleaning them immediately. findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the food handling certification of the PIC. The other employee in the facility had a Food protection manager certification.  PIC told inspector that their certification had expired. PIC  assured inspector that they will get the training for the certification done. Ensure that the certification is acquired to be in compliance with the law. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed open cans of cheese sauce and pizza sauce in the reach in cooler that were not date marked with the date of opening, and a jug of house made Italian dressing that was not date marked with the date of preparation. Date mark all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods with the date of opening of preparation and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed open cans of pizza sauce stored in the reach in cooler. Do not store acidic foods in open cans--always transfer food to a food grade container after opening.
750-130 Ready to eat food shall be stored in a matter to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the knife to be stored in the container of lettuce in the prep cooler with the handle down in contact with the lettuce. Store utensils with the handles extended up and out of food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

No hot water is available in the men's restroom at all and hot water side in the women's restroom is barely warm. Provide hot water to each hand sink.
750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

Outerside of bacon container was in direct contact with lettuce in the pan. Do not store the outer surfaces of food containers in direct contact with other foods. Have a barrier, such as plastic wrap, between the container and the food. B) Lids of multiple #10 cans were soiled with dust, and one marinara can had heavy food debris buildup on it. Clean/sanitize the lids of the cans, and store them so they are protected from food splash/debris.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text: 750.1310 - Spray bottle of bleach water was stored next to food on a shelf above the prep table in back. Spray bottle was moved to proper storage area by 3 part sink. All toxic items must be properly stored segregated from food and all food related items, such as single service items and clean utensils/equipment, to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals. **Make sure bottles are always properly labeled as to their contents**

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Pork in a container in the top portion of the prep cooler was sitting up the top edges of other containers and was not down in the holding area in contact with cold air. Product was at 49F/50F upon arrival of the inspector. The manager stated product had been moved from the lower portion of the cooler to make a sandwich ~15-20 min earlier. Manager was allowed to place the container back in the lower portion and given the benefit of the doubt in terms of the amount of time the product had been out of temperature. The temperature of all other products in the cooler were 41F/below, and the pork went down to 41F quite rapidly. Maintain cold foods at 41F/below, and store containers properly in the top portion of the prep cooler.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Bottom inside the bread warmer had some mold buildup. Foods shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times. Manager cleaned out the bottom of the bread warmer during the inspection. Properly clean the warmer daily to eliminate the buildup of mold and other debris inside.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - Spray bottle and bucket of sanitizer solution used for food contact surfaces were at a concentration above 200ppm chlorine. Test strips turned dark purple to black when solutions were tested. Sanitizer concentration for clean in place equipment (i.e. slicer, etc) must not exceed 100ppm chlorine. A stronger concentration is not better and is considered toxic. Maintain buckets and spray bottles at 100ppm chlorine; sanitizer solution for immersion in the 3 part sink should be 50ppm chlorine. Manager remade the solutions during the inspection to make sure they were at the proper concentration.
